[PS] A. Grothendieck, *Pursuing Stacks (À la poursuite des champs). First episode: the modelizing story* (typescript, 1983), §69; public-domain edition by the scrivener (2015), extended by M. Carmona with U. Buchholtz. arXiv:2111.01000. https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01000

[Gr] M. Groth, *Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 13 (2013), 313–374; arXiv:1112.3840. https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.3840 — the axioms are stated there in the form used here, with the base change morphisms of Section 3.

[Gr] M. Groth, *Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 13 (2013), 313–374; arXiv:1112.3840. https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.3840 — Section 1.2 develops the base change calculus; the pasting lemmas, the finality of right adjoints and the extension by initial and terminal objects appear there.

[PS] A. Grothendieck, *Pursuing Stacks*, §69, arXiv:2111.01000. https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01000 — the assignment \(I\mapsto D(\operatorname{Hom}(I,\mathcal A))\) and the demand that restriction have adjoints on both sides.

[Gr] M. Groth, *Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 13 (2013), 313–374; arXiv:1112.3840. https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.3840 — Section 1.3 proves the derivator property for combinatorial model categories through projective and injective model structures and a discrete-fibration lemma; the argument here follows the same pattern with resolutions instead of model structures.

[Gr] M. Groth, *Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 13 (2013), 313–374; arXiv:1112.3840. https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.3840 — Sections 3 and 4.1: pointed derivators defined by a zero object in the underlying category, cocartesian and cartesian squares, suspension, loops, cones and fibres, stability.

[Gr] M. Groth, *Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 13 (2013), 313–374; arXiv:1112.3840. https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.3840 — Section 3.2: the detection result, which Groth attributes to Franke, and the composition and cancellation of cocartesian squares; Section 1: shifted derivators and the objectwise criterion. The recognition lemma above derives these from a single pasting argument.

[PS] A. Grothendieck, *Pursuing Stacks*, §69, arXiv:2111.01000. https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01000 — the demand that systems of objects of \(\mathbb D(J)\) be objects of a value of \(\mathbb D\), which the shifted derivators answer.

[Gr] M. Groth, *Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 13 (2013), 313–374; arXiv:1112.3840. https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.3840 — Section 4.1: additivity of stable derivators, with semi-additivity from a three-by-three diagram of bicartesian squares and the additive inverse from the action of the symmetric group on three letters on a homotopy limit of a three-legged cospan. The proofs above use instead the coproduct of two degenerate squares, and the collapse maps of a three-legged span, which is the argument showing that a suspension is a co-H-group in homotopy theory.

[Gr] M. Groth, *Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 13 (2013), 313–374; arXiv:1112.3840. https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.3840 — Section 4.2: the canonical triangulated structure, with distinguished triangles from cofibre diagrams, rotation through a diagram on \([2]\times[2]\) without one corner, and the octahedron through a diagram on \([4]\times[2]\) without two corners. The flip lemma (Lemma 2.1) and the explicit bookkeeping of the identifications \(\iota\) are written for this lesson.

[PS] A. Grothendieck, *Pursuing Stacks*, §69, arXiv:2111.01000. https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01000 — the expectation that the triangulated structure of derived categories follows formally from the derivator.

[Gr] M. Groth, *Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 13 (2013), 313–374; arXiv:1112.3840. https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.3840 — Section 4.2: exact morphisms of stable derivators, and the exactness of restriction and homotopy Kan extensions. The comparison with the classical triangles of \(D(R)\), including the sign, is worked out in this lesson.

[PS] A. Grothendieck, *Pursuing Stacks*, §69, arXiv:2111.01000. https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01000 — the expectation that the two Dold–Puppe sequences and the triangulated structure follow formally from the derivator.
